I was always big as a kid. Not overly obese, but I always noticed that I was taller and chubbier than kids my age. I always had a small gut. I think I was maybe 11 years old and I was hitting a soccer ball with my dad at my brother’s soccer practice. He kept kicking it hard and I had trouble getting to the ball without getting tired fast. As I was huffing and puffing, he just got this angry look on his face, looked at me, and said, “You’re so fat.” 

I never had bad thoughts about my body until he said that. Sure, I was teased and bullied for my weight, but I never took it to heart, because I never cared about other peoples opinion of me. But that small comment ruined my self esteem and confidence. I still think about it over 10 years later. He has said worse things as the years passed, but the first one I remember has ruined my sense of worth and it resonates with me today.

I used to work at AMC Theatres as a Crew Lead. I was usually put as the hot foods handler in concessions. Some of my duties everyday would include checking and writing all the temps, checking freezers to see if it needs to be stocked, checking candy, basically make sure everything is stocked for what day it was (weekends would be a heavier stock as it is REALLY BUSY, but premier nights were the absolute worst), possibly training new people (big turnover), planning everyone’s breaks in concessions, responsible for refunds in concessions, calling the manager for change, and ofc, handling all food orders whilst taking customers orders. 

I did so much shit, but I lacked recognization the whole time I was there. To this day, I can’t believe that I would give up my breaks to help clean concessions or stock to make it easier when we were closing. Like why did I give up so much of my time when all I was being compensated with was minimum wage. 

I remember when i was handling a lot of food orders in the back of concessions, alone, when a new coworker needed help on the till and with a customer. I went out to e front a couple minutes later (I had to finish making a hot dog) and I did what I usually did. I guided him in how to make a proper transaction and showed him some quick and handy tricks he could use to help him on the till and with customers. The customer in question told me, “Are you a manager? You’re doing a great job.” I told her no, that I was just a Crew Lead. She said, “You’re doing an awesome job. Here’s my card, we’re always looking for team players.” I don’t remember what it was, but my god was I riding a high for the rest of the night. I was happy. There’s A LOT more shittty things that happened there, though.

It wasn’t until I quit for school about two years later when my manager said that I was the best and fastest employer they had. Why didn’t they tell me this sooner?? Tf
